chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Shihab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who freed a slave of his on the eve of Arafat: Would a Hajj suffice for the slave, a Hajj of Al-Islam? He said: Yes. I said: So if a mother of a child is taken to Hajj by her master, would it suffice from her? He said: No. I said: Is there any recompense for him regarding her Hajj? He said: Yes.

He said: And I asked him about a boy of ten years performing Hajj. He said: Upon him is the Hajj of Al-Islam when he attains puberty, and similar to that is the girl, upon her would be the Hajj when she menstruates.

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (a female slave who bears her master's child)
key_terms.احْتَلَمَ: Attained puberty (specifically via nocturnal emission for males)

ai.seo_question: Does freeing a slave on the eve of Arafat exempt the master from performing his obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal nuances of Hajj sufficiency by distinguishing between the master's obligation and the slave's status, noting that while freeing a slave on Arafat does not exempt the master, the master retains reward for a slave woman's Hajj. It further establishes the rite of passage for children, linking the validity of their Hajj to the onset of puberty (bulugh) via specific biological signs, a key criterion in Shia fiqh for determining legal responsibility (taklif).
